1. 빌레몬서 기록 배경\n 1) 빌레몬에 대해서\n - 에베소, 골로새:
1. Background of the writing of Philemon
 1) About Philemon
 - Tychicus carries three letters: Ephesians, Colossians, Philemon.
 - Philemon was a man who learned the Bible from the apostle Paul in the school of Tyrannus, became a minister, and was running a house church. His son was Archippus.
 2) Why Philemon was written
 - In the house of the minister Philemon there was a slave named Onesimus, who took some money and ran away to Rome. In those days, a slave running all the way to Rome was a huge event. Someone this smart shouldn't have been a slave.
로마까지 도망가서는 바울을 만나가지고 예수님을 만나서 완전히 거듭나게 되: He ran all the way to Rome, met Paul, met Jesus, was completely born again, and became a different person. With an Onesimus like that, people like us would say, 'If you go home you'll be beaten to death, so stay with me,' but Paul isn't like that.
네가 지은 죄를 예수님께서 용서하셨다고 하더라도 반드시 주인에게 용서를: He sends him back, saying that even though Jesus has forgiven the sin you committed, you must still be forgiven by your master. Christianity has never taught, once God forgives you, that's all there is to it.
이런 도망간 노예들은 잡히면 보통 주인이 십자가에 못 박아 버립니다. 그: Runaway slaves like this, when caught, were usually nailed to a cross by their masters. So from the point of view of Onesimus going back, too, he's going at the risk of his life. So Paul writes him a letter.
2. 빌레몬서 내용\n - 아무튼 골로새서를 전달하고 빌레몬 목사의 집에:
2. The content of Philemon
 - Anyway, after delivering Colossians, Tychicus goes to the house of Pastor Philemon and reads the letter.
 - First he greets Philemon, his wife Apphia, and his son Archippus, and then instead of going straight to the main point, he heaps praise on Philemon's faith and love.
4내가 항상 내 하나님께 감사하고 기도할 때에 너를 말함은 5주 예수와: 4I thank my God, making mention of thee always in my prayers, 5Hearing of thy love and faith, which thou hast toward the Lord Jesus, and toward all saints; 6That the communication of thy faith may become effectual by the acknowledging of every good thing which is in you in Christ Jesus. 7For we have great joy and consolation in thy love, because the bowels of the saints are refreshed by thee, brother.
붕 띄워 놓고는 본론: Butters him up, then gets to the point
8이러므로 내가 그리스도 안에서 아주 담대하게 네게 마땅한 일로 명할 수: 8Wherefore, though I might be much bold in Christ to enjoin thee that which is convenient,
9도리어 사랑으로써 간구하노라 빌레몬이 바울의 제자이기 때문에 얼마든지: 9Yet for love's sake I rather beseech thee, Since Philemon is Paul's disciple, he could command him as much as he wants, but he appeals in love. being such an one as Paul the aged, and now also a prisoner of Jesus Christ. Old and in prison. Putting on the pressure subtly, isn't he?
10갇힌 중에서 낳은 아들 오네시모를 위하여 네게 간구하노라: 10I beseech thee for my son Onesimus, whom I have begotten in my bonds:
11그가 전에는 네게 무익하였으나 이제는 나와 네게 유익하므로 무익이라는: 11Which in time past was to thee unprofitable, but now profitable to thee and to me: The word for unprofitable is 'kanesimo', and the word for profitable is Onesimus.
12네게 그를 돌려 보내노니 그는 내 심복이라: 12Whom I have sent again: thou therefore receive him, that is, mine own bowels:
13그를 내게 머물러 있게 하여 내 복음을 위하여 갇힌 중에서 네 대신: 13Whom I would have retained with me, that in thy stead he might have ministered unto me in the bonds of the gospel:
14다만 네 승낙이 없이는 내가 아무 것도 하기를 원하지 아니하노니 이는: 14But without thy mind would I do nothing; that thy benefit should not be as it were of necessity, but willingly. He's already been using him that way, and then he says he won't do anything without your consent. Paul is a real pro at tightening the screws on people, isn't he?
15아마 그가 잠시 떠나게 된 것은 너로 하여금 그를 영원히 두게 함이리: 15For perhaps he therefore departed for a season, that thou shouldest receive him for ever; The fact that he ran away, in the end, seems to have been so that he could be with you forever. He really defends him, doesn't he?
16이 후로는 종과 같이 대하지 아니하고 종 이상으로 곧 사랑 받는 형제: 16Not now as a servant, but above a servant, a brother beloved, specially to me, but how much more unto thee, both in the flesh, and in the Lord? From now on, don't treat him like a slave; treat him like a brother. He and I are already like brothers. It drives a person crazy, doesn't it?
17그러므로 네가 나를 동역자로 알진대 그를 영접하기를 내게 하듯 하고: 17If thou count me therefore a partner, receive him as myself.
18그가 만일 네게 불의를 하였거나 네게 빚진 것이 있으면 그것을 내 앞: 18If he hath wronged thee, or oweth thee ought, put that on mine account;
19나 바울이 친필로 쓰노니 내가 갚으려니와 네가 이 외에 네 자신이 내: 19I Paul have written it with mine own hand, I will repay it: albeit I do not say to thee how thou owest unto me even thine own self besides. You owe me a debt of the gospel too, don't you? But I won't mention that.
20오 형제여 나로 주 안에서 너로 말미암아 기쁨을 얻게 하고 내 마음이: 20Yea, brother, let me have joy of thee in the Lord: refresh my bowels in the Lord.
21나는 네가 순종할 것을 확신하므로 네게 썼노니 네가 내가 말한 것보다: 21Having confidence in thy obedience I wrote unto thee, knowing that thou wilt also do more than I say. He leaves him no room to wiggle, doesn't he?
22오직 너는 나를 위하여 숙소를 마련하라 너희 기도로 내가 너희에게 나: 22But withal prepare me also a lodging: for I trust that through your prayers I shall be given unto you. What does it mean, prepare a lodging? It's like, I'm going to come and see.
23그리스도 예수 안에서 나와 함께 갇힌 자 에바브라와: 23There salute thee Epaphras, my fellowprisoner in Christ Jesus;
25우리 주 예수 그리스도의 은혜가 너희 심령과 함께 있을지어다: 25The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.
